title: Quantify and Alert on KV/Prefix Cache-induced Non-determinism Across Model/Config Changes
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Build a reproducible harness and CI checks that quantify when KV/prefix cache hits cause output changes (non-determinism or quality regressions) after model or config updates. The goal is to measure and attribute differences to cache behavior (hit vs miss) and to surface high-confidence alerts when differences exceed product thresholds so engineers can triage before deployments reach customers.
acceptance_criteria: Determinism test: for any supported model/config, same request with cache enabled vs disabled produces diffs measured by token-level and semantic metrics (edit distance, normalized BLEU, embedding cosine) and results are recorded
Automated CI job that runs on PRs touching runtime cache code or model packaging, failing when regression thresholds exceeded
Root-cause signal: output diffs are attributed to (a) cache keying bug, (b) kernel scheduling/quantization side-effect, or (c) expected behavior from model change — with links to evidence
Dashboard: weekly summary of cache-hit vs cache-miss deltas, top offending prompts, and regression trendlines
Runbook: steps for triage with reproducible reproduction commands and suggested mitigations (config toggles, rolling back quantization, model pinning)
tests_and_datasets: synthetic suite: deterministic_prefixes_gen_v1 (covers varied lengths, multi-turn contexts, embedded instrumented markers)
metrics: token_edit_rate: normalized Levenshtein / generated token count
semantic_shift: 1 - cosine(embedding(cache_hit), embedding(cache_miss)) using embed-model v2
functional_change_rate: percentage of outputs that change top-1 intent label (intent classifier)
false_positive_rate of CI alerts measured on historical backtests
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument runtime to produce deterministic trace pairs: same request with cache forced-hit and cache-disabled in same container. Store (request, response_hit, response_miss, metadata)
2) Build a lightweight comparison service that computes metrics above and persists results to eval DB
3) Create CI integration: a PR check that replays a fixed seed subset of dataset across changed binaries/configs — fail on regression_score > 0.12
4) Dashboard + alert: create Grafana panels and an alerting rule mapping to PagerDuty for P0 regressions and Slack for P1
5) Add automatic attribution heuristics: compare diffs across quantization profiles and kernel flags to suggest likely cause
6) Add a developer-facing reproduction CLI: redwood-eval reproduce --id <trace_id> --mode {hit,miss}
blockers: Non-deterministic kernel scheduling on newer CUDA drivers makes hit/miss comparisons noisy; need controlled environment or deterministic seeds
Missing stable embed-model for semantic similarity — design decision required whether to freeze embed-model in evaluation or allow upgrades
Storage quota for trace pairs in eval DB — need approval for additional S3/eval DB space (ticket ENG-9910 request pending)
dependencies: runtime-ops: deploy a deterministic test-slab image in staging
security-review: confirm storage of deidentified customer prompts (privacy/compliance)
